header_facts: GGUF v3, arch qwen3next, 843 tensors, 52 keys, header 6.0 MB (fit in the 32 MiB range fetch). 48 blocks, all MoE (no dense blocks): 512 experts, 10 used, expert FFN 512, shared expert FFN 512. Hybrid attention: full_attention_interval 4, so 12 full-attention layers (GQA, 16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, key_length 256, value_length 256) and 36 Gated DeltaNet layers (ssm conv_kernel 4, inner_size 4096, state_size 128, group_count 16, time_step_rank 32). No sliding window. n_embd 2048, rope base 5e6, native context 262144. Vocab 151936 (qwen2 BPE), much smaller than the 248k of Qwen3.6/3.8. Tensors 35.784 GiB: IQ3_S 20.62, IQ4_XS 12.75, Q8_0 1.98, Q6_K 0.24, F32 0.19. Experts 33.375 GiB, 0.6953 GiB (712 MiB) per block, uniform across blocks 0-47. Non-expert GPU weights 2.102 GiB (block tensors 1.864 plus output/norm 0.238). token_embd 0.308 GiB on the host. GGUF embeds general.sampling temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 40. Chat template 6055 chars with <tool_call>, <function=, <parameter=, and no think tags.
kv_math: KV (full-attention layers only): 12 layers x 2 KV heads x (256+256) x 1.0625 B x 131072 = 1.594 GiB (1632 MiB) for q8_0; f16 would be 3.0 GiB. Per token: 24 KiB f16, 12.75 KiB q8_0. Recurrent state at b12407 (src/llama-hparams.cpp n_embd_r/n_embd_s, f32): conv = (4-1) x (4096 + 2x16x128) = 24576 floats; ssm = 128 x 4096 = 524288 floats; (24576+524288) x 4 B = 2.10 MiB per DeltaNet layer x 36 = 75.4 MiB for -np 1, covered by the 0.8 GiB overhead allowance. At 262144 the q8_0 KV would be 3.19 GiB. Host-side prompt state for one full 131k prompt is about 1.59 GiB KV plus 75 MiB recurrent, and each context checkpoint is about 75 MiB (up to 32 per slot, about 2.4 GiB worst case).

recommended.vram_breakdown: non-expert weights 2.102 GiB = 2152 MiB; experts of blocks 38-47 on GPU 10 x 712 = 7120 MiB; KV q8_0 at 131072 = 1632 MiB; --moe-cache-mib 3328 MiB; overhead (CUDA context, compute buffers at -ub 512, 75 MiB recurrent state) 0.8 GiB = 819 MiB; llama-server total 15051 MiB; desktop 112 MiB. Overhead kept at 0.8 GiB: the 152k vocab shrinks the logits buffer by about 190 MiB versus the 248k Qwen models, but 48 layers, 512 experts and a 712 MiB per-block expert upload in prefill may grow other buffers, so no reduction is taken.

alternative: --n-cpu-moe 36 --moe-cache-mib 1920 (12 GPU blocks 8544 MiB plus 1920 MiB cache; predicted nvidia-smi peak 15179 MiB, 662 MiB free; pinned experts 25.03 GiB, container about 31.8 GiB, --memory 33g). Worth one short run because with 512 experts and 10 used the 3328 MiB cache covers only about 63 of 512 experts per RAM block (about 12%, against about 28% on Qwen3.6), so whole blocks may beat the cache here, and the split also cuts 1.4 GiB of pinned RAM and about 5% of the per-ubatch prefill upload.
thinking: none. The model card says it supports only non-thinking mode and emits no <think> blocks, and the GGUF template has no think tags or enable_thinking switch, so --reasoning auto detects nothing and no server flag is needed (--reasoning off is harmless but unnecessary). There is no per-request switch; OpenCode gets reasoning supported false and no variants.
tool_calling: Native via --jinja: the GGUF template contains <tool_call>, <function= and <parameter= and does not contain the excluded no-newline form "'<tool_call><function=' ~ tool_call.name ~ '>'", so common/chat.cpp at b12407 (lines 1420-1427) selects common_chat_params_init_qwen3_coder, the Qwen3-Coder XML parser, and calls come back as OpenAI tool_calls. Template is the Unsloth upload from the 2026-03-06 repo state (sha ce09c67b), after their tool-call and key_gdiff fixes. Run the scripted tool-call smoke test (finish_reason tool_calls) before OpenCode use.
sampling: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 40 (Qwen model card line 194, also embedded in the GGUF as general.sampling.*), min_p 0.01 per the Unsloth page (llama.cpp default 0.05), repeat penalty off (llama.cpp default 1.0). Passed explicitly as --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40 --min-p 0.01. Card example uses max_tokens 65536.
expected_speed: Decode about 60-95 tok/s (estimate). Reasoning: the GPU reads about 2.1 GiB of non-expert weights plus about 0.65 GiB of active experts per token (about 3 ms at 896 GB/s) over 48 layers with CUDA graphs disabled, and Qwen3.6 with 40 layers ran 8.3 ms/token at 83% cache hits; here the cache covers a smaller share of 512 experts, so expect a lower hit rate (perhaps 55-70%) and more PCIe uploads of about 14 MiB per RAM block per token at misses. Prefill at 8k about 700-850 tok/s (estimate): large batches upload every used expert, nearly all 512 per block, so each 512-token ubatch moves about 26.4 GiB from pinned RAM; Qwen3.6 moved 10.5 GiB per ubatch at 2112 tok/s, which implies about 43 GB/s, giving 512 / (26.4 GiB / 43 GB/s) = about 840 tok/s as the upper bound. A 30k prompt then takes about 40 s and 100k about 2-2.5 min.

issues.note: CUDA VMM-pool OOM during prompt processing aborts the server; --fit refuses to trim once -ngl is set by the user. Relevant because this plan pins -ngl all, so an overshoot is a SIGABRT, not a refit; keep the 500 MiB margin and raise --n-cpu-moe or lower the cache on failure.
IQ3_S garbage with self-built nvcc 13.2.0/13.2.1 on Blackwell; 20.62 GiB of this file is IQ3_S. The CUDA 12.8.1 image should be unaffected, but check the first answers for garbage.
Offloaded-MoE prefill waits on serial expert H2D copies; with 38 blocks in RAM this dominates prefill even with -lm none.

kb_discrepancies: Memory estimate is too high: the recipe says the GPU holds about 13.2 GiB plus about 0.4 GiB CUDA context at --n-cpu-moe 37 (at-a-glance: about 13.6). Header: 7.648 GiB GPU experts + 2.102 GiB non-expert + 1.594 GiB q8_0 KV = 11.344 GiB, plus the measured-family overhead of about 0.8 GiB (not 0.4) = about 12.1 GiB; about 3 GiB of VRAM is left unused at 37.

The 262k note is wrong: at --n-cpu-moe 37 with q8_0 KV, 262144 needs 7.648 + 2.102 + 3.188 + 0.8 = about 13.7 GiB, which fits with about 1.4 GiB to spare; it is not marginal and does not need --n-cpu-moe 38 or --fit.
The recipe predates the MoE expert cache findings: it has no -lm none, no -t 8 and no --moe-cache-mib, which on Qwen3.6 doubled prefill and nearly doubled decode (llamacpp/README.md lines 172-190).

Speed is stale: '30-50 tok/s inferred' assumes mmap'd experts and no cache; with pinned experts and a VRAM cache the estimate is about 60-95 tok/s, and prefill is upload-bound at about 840 tok/s rather than limited by pageable memory (#25859 cited for pageable copies, but -lm none pins them).

--cache-ram 2048 holds only one full 131k prompt state (about 1.59 GiB KV plus 75 MiB recurrent); OpenCode title and subagent requests would evict the main conversation. 4096 is a better fit and is budgeted in the 35g cap.
The run command still uses -hf with HF_TOKEN and a /root/.cache mount without --user; the README's tested variant (--user, /hf mount) and the lead's -m path supersede it.

The 32g cap with --cache-ram 2048 leaves little room once checkpoints are counted: 25.7 GiB pinned at 37 blocks + 0.31 token_embd + 2.0 cache + 2-2.5 process and up to 2.4 GiB checkpoints is about 30-32 GiB.

#31974 is cited as support for letting --fit choose at 262k, but the issue is about a VMM-pool OOM abort; its relevant point is the opposite caution that --fit will not trim anything once -ngl is set.
Minor: the chat.cpp link points at b12418 while the image is b12407; the Qwen3-Coder detection at lines 1420-1427 is identical at b12407 (verified).
risks: Pinned RAM: -lm none page-locks 26.42 GiB of experts plus 0.31 GiB token_embd; predicted container about 33.2 GiB (26.73 pinned + 4.0 prompt cache + about 2.5 process and checkpoints) under a 35g cap, leaving about 5-7 GiB of the roughly 40 GiB free for the desktop. Close large applications and run no heavy gate at the same time; pinned pages cannot be reclaimed, so systemd-oomd pressure falls on everything else.

Overhead uncertainty: 0.8 GiB is extrapolated from Qwen3.6/3.8; a larger prefill staging buffer for the 712 MiB per-block expert upload could eat into the 678 MiB margin. Read the load log and nvidia-smi during the 100k probe; on OOM lower --moe-cache-mib by 512 first.
Cache hit rate may be well below Qwen3.6's 83% because routing spreads over 512 experts with 10 active; run with -lv 4 to log the hit rate at exit and compare against the 36/1920 alternative.

Prefill is upload-bound at about 840 tok/s with -ub 512; a larger -ub (1024 or 2048) would amortise each 26 GiB upload over more tokens and could roughly double or quadruple prefill, but its compute-buffer VRAM is unmeasured, so leave it for a follow-up run.
q8_0 KV may cost decode speed on CUDA (#27623, fix PR #31802 open per the KB); only 12 layers carry KV so the penalty should be small, but f16 (3.0 GiB) would need about 1.4 GiB less cache.
IQ3_S tensors (20.62 GiB) are the class hit by #28581; the CUDA 12.8.1 image should be fine but sanity-check the first answers.
Hybrid DeltaNet model: keep default --ctx-checkpoints (do not set 0) and expect #30357 style re-prefills; at about 840 tok/s a full re-prefill of 100k costs about 2 minutes, so watch timings.cache_n.
